scope: Explicit whole45-layer GLM request/executor from token IDs through final logits and greedy decode

execution.ownership: Immutable backend model resources; resident request owns all GPU allocations/bank streams/pins/BLAS; separate host metadata released after device work drains.
execution.transaction: Begin copies IDs and scheduler metadata, submits embedding; submit retains exact layer/MoE continuation on BUSY; final successful fence commits every recurrent/history/tail parity and request position together. Partial failure poisons the request; healthy idle restart clears state without allocation.
execution.final_head: Normalize all prompt rows, rawQ8 head only final sampled row.

faults_tested: Device/host one-byte-short admission without GPU allocation
Allocation17 failure leaves no GPU or execution resource owner
Pending transaction rejects restart, begin and premature complete
Forced expert-bank BUSY retains all previous attention work
All logits exactly replay after healthy restart
Failed final fence leaves old logical position/parity and poisons request

source_io.measurement: Actual CPU expert-source read bytes; not an isolated GPU DMA stall or residency benchmark.

oracle.inputs: Actual checkpoint token IDs, independent original embedding and all45 original block computations; no injected native activation, routing choice or weight tensor.
oracle.experts: Full288-expert raw tensor domains; only original router-selected rows populated before unchanged original vector operators. Selected IDs above255 retained. Checkpoint clamp10 explicit.
oracle.arithmetic_profile: Original rawGGUF operators; fused-recurrent KDA; default deferred/fused mHC; short causal NoPE MLA; original identity-projection materialized K/V; BF16 gamma/RMS and final-row Q8 head; default non-batch-invariant normalization launch.
oracle.repeats: Every original full-model schedule captured twice; every layer tuple and logits exact across original repeats and independent native execution.

sanitizer_environment.initial_failure: Default ASan shadow-gap protection made CUDA device enumeration return error2/out of memory, reproduced by a tiny standalone cudaGetDeviceCount ASan probe before model code. Disabling shadow-gap protection made the probe and actual request sanitizer run pass. Original failed logs retained.

backend.gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition

limits: Whole-model independent cases are prefill1/decode1 and prefill9/decode1; chunked/resumed prefill and long-context whole-model cases remain pending.
Persistent state exactness is separately covered by component references; current whole-model comparison checks all45 deferred tuples and final heads plus functional decode continuation.
Long sparse chronological ordering versus original nondeterministic atomic ordering remains unqualified through generation.
Original default chunk-KDA, whole-plugin/HF merged loader, automatic generation admission, serving concurrency and vLLM performance parity are not claimed.
Whole-model kernel/transfer/fence trace remains pending; test-only tuple readbacks are outside the engine API.
